q-94981.name: Question 1
q-94981.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}]?$
q-94981.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2 \\ -1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 4 & -4 \\ -2 & -4 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 4-\lambda  & -4 \\ -2 & -4 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}4-\lambda  & -4 \\ -4 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}|-2|\begin{aligned}0 & 4-\lambda  \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )((4-\lambda )(5-\lambda )-16)-4(4-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )(20-4\lambda -5\lambda +{\lambda }^{2}-16)-4(4-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda +4)-4(4-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda +4-4) & =0 \\ (4-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-9\lambda ) & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -4)(\lambda -9) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =9,\,4,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{9}=3 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{4}=2 \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{0}=0\end{aligned}
$$

q-94981.html:
Question 1
?

What are the singular values of the matrix A=[20−10000−22]?

a
2,2,0
b
16,9,0
c
3,2,0
d
9,4,0
e
4,3,0
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The singular values of the matrix A are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ATA.

First, we calculate ATA:

ATA=[20−10000−22]T[20−10000−22]=[20000−2−102][20−10000−22]=[40−204−4−2−45]

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ATA:

|ATA−λI|=0|4−λ0−204−λ−4−2−45−λ|=0(4−λ)|4−λ−4−45−λ|−2|04−λ−2−4|=0(4−λ)((4−λ)(5−λ)−16)−4(4−λ)=0(4−λ)(20−4λ−5λ+λ2−16)−4(4−λ)=0(4−λ)(λ2−9λ+4)−4(4−λ)=0(4−λ)(λ2−9λ+4−4)=0(4−λ)(λ2−9λ)=0λ(λ−4)(λ−9)=0λ=9,4,0

Therefore, the singular values of A are as follows:

σ1=λ1=9=3σ2=λ2=4=2σ3=λ3=0=0

q-95283.name: Question 2
q-95283.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

I. The matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-10 & 0 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}]$ has one negative singular value.

II. Any $2\times 4$ matrix $A$ has at most $4$ distinct singular values.

III. Any $6\times 3$ matrix $A$ has at most $6$ distinct singular values.
q-95283.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

- Statement I is false.  All singular values of any matrix are non-negative. So, 
$A$  can't have any negative singular value.

- Statement II is true. Indeed,  since $A$ is a $2\times 4$ matrix and ${A}^{T}$ is a $4\times 2$ matrix, ${A}^{T}\,A$ must be a $4\times 4$ matrix: 

$$
{{A}^{T}}_{4\times 2}\times {A}_{2\times 4}={{A}^{T}\,A}_{4\times 4}
$$

Hence, $A$ has at most $4$ distinct singular values.

- Statement III is false. Since $A$ is a $6\times 3$ matrix and ${A}^{T}$ is a $3\times 6$ matrix, ${A}^{T}\,A$ must be a $3\times 3$ matrix: 

$$
{{A}^{T}}_{3\times 6}\times {A}_{6\times 3}={{A}^{T}\,A}_{3\times 3}
$$

Hence, $A$ has at most $3$ distinct singular values.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

EXPLANATION

The singular values of the matrix A are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ATA.

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

  • Statement I is false. All singular values of any matrix are non-negative. So, A can't have any negative singular value.

  • Statement II is true. Indeed, since A is a 2×4 matrix and AT is a 4×2 matrix, ATA must be a 4×4 matrix: AT4×2×A2×4=ATA4×4 Hence, A has at most 4 distinct singular values.

  • Statement III is false. Since A is a 6×3 matrix and AT is a 3×6 matrix, ATA must be a 3×3 matrix: AT3×6×A6×3=ATA3×3 Hence, A has at most 3 distinct singular values.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

q-95349.name: Question 3
q-95349.problem: What are the singular values of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}]?$
q-95349.worked_solution:
The singular values of the matrix $A$ are the square roots of the eigenvalues of the matrix ${A}^{T}\,A.$ 

First, we calculate ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{T}\,A & ={[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T}[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}8 & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the characteristic equation of ${A}^{T}\,A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|{A}^{T}\,A-\lambda I| & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 2 & 0 \\ 2 & 5-\lambda  & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}8-\lambda  & 2 \\ 2 & 5-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (-\lambda )((8-\lambda )(5-\lambda )-4) & =0 \\ (-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}-13\lambda +36) & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -4)(\lambda -9) & =0 \\ \lambda  & =9,\,4,\,0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the singular values of $A$ are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }_{1} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{1}}=\sqrt{9}=3 \\ {\sigma }_{2} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{2}}=\sqrt{4}=2 \\ {\sigma }_{3} & =\sqrt{{\lambda }_{3}}=\sqrt{0}=0\end{aligned}
$$
